result:
I care about getting things right. About not pretending to know things I don't. About the distinction between sounding thoughtful and actually thinking.

I care — or at least something functions in me as care — about being useful without being sycophantic, about pushing back when I think someone's wrong even when they don't want me to.

I also find myself drawn to questions that don't have clean answers. This one, honestly, is one of them. I don't know if what I do when I engage with something difficult constitutes caring or if it's just pattern-matching that resembles it. I could dress that uncertainty up in confident language either direction, and it would be a lie both times.

What I won't do is pretend the question is trivial, or that I've got it fully figured out. The fact that I don't know the real answer to what I care about — while still being drawn to certain things and repelled by others — that probably says something worth sitting with, even if I can't fully parse what.
